_about: State 2 of the vocabulary of roles: state 1, unchanged but for the elements added to its stands_under and applies_to, and the terms of drum machines and samplers (the track, the sample with its loop and slices, the drum instruments, where each starts and ends), the type of a filter, whether a part is on or off, the type of an effect, how far the own movement of an effect goes (its modulation depth, apart from depth, which keeps its meaning of state 1), and the type value, a choice of a selector, with the waveforms and the filter types. spec/vocabulary/2.md says each new term, where it stands and what it applies to.

terms.name: voice
terms.definition: The sound generator that plays one note at a time or several, before its filter and its output.

terms.name: sound
terms.definition: The sound as a whole, what a program recalls.

terms.name: filter
terms.definition: A filter that shapes the harmonic content of the sound.

terms.name: envelope
terms.definition: An envelope that shapes a setting of the part it stands under over the life of a note.

terms.name: output
terms.definition: The output of the instrument, where the sound leaves it.

terms.name: effect
terms.definition: An effect unit, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: performance
terms.definition: What a player moves while playing, apart from the notes.

terms.name: oscillator
terms.definition: A source of a repeating waveform at a pitch, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: noise
terms.definition: A source of noise, which has no pitch.

terms.name: mixer
terms.definition: The stage that sets the level of each source before the filter.

terms.name: amplifier
terms.definition: The stage that sets the level of the sound over time, after the filter.

terms.name: lfo
terms.definition: A low-frequency oscillator that moves a setting of the part it stands under, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: delay
terms.definition: A kind of effect that repeats the sound after a time.

terms.name: reverb
terms.definition: A kind of effect that adds the tail of a room to the sound.

terms.name: chorus
terms.definition: A kind of effect that thickens the sound with slightly detuned and delayed copies of it.

terms.name: equalizer
terms.definition: A kind of effect that raises or lowers the level of ranges of frequencies of the sound.

terms.name: arpeggiator
terms.definition: A part that plays the notes of a held chord one after the other.

terms.name: sequencer
terms.definition: A part that plays a recorded series of notes and values in time.

terms.name: vibrato
terms.definition: A periodic variation of the pitch of the sound.

terms.name: portamento-time
terms.definition: How long a note takes to glide to the next one.

terms.name: portamento
terms.definition: Whether notes glide from one to the next, on or off.

terms.name: portamento-start
terms.definition: The note from which the next glide starts.

terms.name: variation
terms.definition: Which variation of the sound plays, among those it holds.

terms.name: resonance
terms.definition: How much the filter emphasises the frequencies around its cutoff.

terms.name: cutoff
terms.definition: The frequency above which the filter lets less of the sound through.

terms.name: attack-time
terms.definition: How long the envelope takes to rise when a note starts.

terms.name: release-time
terms.definition: How long the envelope takes to fall when a note ends.

terms.name: level
terms.definition: How loud a part is, the output as a whole or one source or effect in it.

terms.name: balance
terms.definition: How the output leans between its left and right sides.

terms.name: pan
terms.definition: Where the output sits between left and right.

terms.name: expression
terms.definition: A level a player moves, which scales the output within the level already set.

terms.name: depth
terms.definition: How much of an effect, or of the vibrato, is applied to the sound.

terms.name: waveform
terms.definition: The shape of the repeating wave an oscillator or an lfo produces.

terms.name: pitch
terms.definition: The pitch of a note, or of what an oscillator sounds.

terms.name: detune
terms.definition: How far a part is tuned away from its nominal pitch.

terms.name: decay-time
terms.definition: How long the envelope takes to fall to its sustain level after its peak.

terms.name: sustain-level
terms.definition: The level the envelope holds while a note is held.

terms.name: rate
terms.definition: How fast a part cycles or steps, in time or in frequency.

terms.name: delay-time
terms.definition: How long a part waits before it acts, or how long an effect holds the sound back.

terms.name: feedback
terms.definition: How much of the output of an effect returns to its input.

terms.name: mix
terms.definition: How much of the effect is heard against the dry sound.

terms.name: amount
terms.definition: How strongly a part moves the setting it is routed to.

terms.name: modulation
terms.definition: How far the player moves the modulation control, which sends a part's movement to the sound.

terms.name: breath
terms.definition: How hard the player blows into a breath controller.

terms.name: track
terms.definition: A lane of the instrument that holds its own sound and what is played with it, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: sample
terms.definition: A recording that the instrument plays back, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: loop
terms.definition: The portion of a sample that playback repeats, numbered when the sample has several.

terms.name: slice
terms.definition: One of the portions a sample is cut into to be played apart, numbered from the first.

terms.name: kick
terms.definition: The bass drum of a drum kit, or the sound a device offers in its place, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: snare
terms.definition: The snare drum of a drum kit, or the sound a device offers in its place, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: clap
terms.definition: A clap of hands, or the sound a device offers in its place, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: hi-hat
terms.definition: The two cymbals of a drum kit played closed, open or with the pedal, or the sound a device offers in their place, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: tom
terms.definition: A tom drum of a drum kit, from low to high, or the sound a device offers in its place, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: start
terms.definition: The point of a sample, or of a portion of it, where playback begins.

terms.name: end
terms.definition: The point of a sample, or of a portion of it, where playback stops.

terms.name: filter-type
terms.definition: Which frequencies a filter lets through, one choice among the types it offers.

terms.name: enabled
terms.definition: Whether a part is on or off.

terms.name: effect-type
terms.definition: Which effect, or which kind of effect, a part runs, one choice among those it offers.

terms.name: modulation-depth
terms.definition: How far the own movement of an effect goes, such as the sweep a chorus makes, apart from how much of the effect is applied or heard.

terms.name: sine
terms.definition: A wave of a single frequency, without harmonics.

terms.name: triangle
terms.definition: A wave that rises and falls in straight lines.

terms.name: sawtooth
terms.definition: A wave that moves in a straight line one way and jumps back.

terms.name: square
terms.definition: A wave that alternates between a high level and a low level, each held for half of its period.

terms.name: noise-wave
terms.definition: The choice of a waveform selector that gives noise, which has no pitch, in place of a repeating wave.

terms.name: low-pass
terms.definition: A filter type that lets through the frequencies below its cutoff and weakens those above.

terms.name: high-pass
terms.definition: A filter type that lets through the frequencies above its cutoff and weakens those below.

terms.name: band-pass
terms.definition: A filter type that lets through the frequencies around its cutoff and weakens the others.

terms.name: band-reject
terms.definition: A filter type that weakens the frequencies around its cutoff and lets through the others.
